title: China-to-Moldova EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Redesign — GB/T 20234 versus IEC 62196 Type 2 and CCS2
rows.target_requirement: Moldova deployments commonly follow the European IEC ecosystem for EV charging where IEC 62196 Type 2 is used for AC and CCS2 for DC fast charging when specified by operator, fleet, project, or regulation. For Moldova, IEC Type 2/CCS2 compatibility should be verified against site procurement and interconnection requirements, not treated as an automatic legal approval by itself.
target_standards: Project, fleet, operator, or public-procurement connector requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China references typically use GB/T 20234.2 for AC and GB/T 20234.3 for DC connectors. These references are useful baselines but must be converted where Moldova projects specify Type 2 or CCS2, including locking logic, communication interfaces, and safety revalidation.
rows.gap: Design and procurement actions for Moldova-bound chargers usually include connector conversion, pilot and proximity logic verification, cable thermal approvals, lock and safety interlock checks, station label updates, and post-redesign commissioning evidence.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where project procurement, operator, or fleet specifies Type 2 / CCS2; otherwise interoperability expectation only
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — GB/T 20234 is China baseline only and does not confirm Type 2 or CCS2 compatibility for Moldova

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not present GB/T 20234 hardware as Type 2 / CCS2 ready for Moldova projects. Build connector and communication evidence around the declared Moldova project interface specification.

rows.requirement: ANRE and Moldelectrica Project Grid-Connection and Service Approval
rows.target_requirement: Moldova EV charging sites generally require project-level interconnection review by ANRE and relevant network operators before energization. Charging points may need technical acceptance, protection settings, metering agreements, and dispatch or balancing coordination even when product conformity is already documented.
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese utility and project documents under GB/T 19964-2024 can support design review, but they do not substitute ANRE/Moldelectrica grid-connection or charging service approval in Moldova.
china_standards: State Grid / China Southern Power Grid project procedures
rows.gap: Prepare Moldova interconnection documentation for each site including charger model and software version, grid-code compliance settings, frequency and voltage behavior for 230/400 V 50 Hz sites, remote-control and metering interfaces, energization sequence, and acceptance sign-off language.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for charging projects that require ANRE interconnection and network-operator acceptance, including energized operations and commercial commissioning
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — Chinese project tests are preparatory only for Moldova grid interconnection

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm grid-connection scope, energization sequence, and acceptance criteria with ANRE or the local operator before declaring Moldova-ready deployment.

rows.requirement: China GB/T EV Charger Baseline versus Moldova Market-Access Package
rows.target_requirement: Moldova EV access readiness is typically a combined package covering CE-aligned product evidence, EN/TS EN IEC safety and EMC support, ANRE market and interconnection rules, Moldelectrica and local operator documentation, OCPP or backend obligations, and site documentation including labeling and manuals in local acceptance languages.
target_standards: CE technical file and declaration route
ANRE EV interconnection and market requirements
Moldova operator-side commissioning and backend acceptance
rows.china_equivalent: China documents usually start with GB/T 18487.1, GB/T 20234, and GB/T 27930, plus CCC or domestic certification. Those are useful for mapping but should be treated as baseline documents only unless project-specific Moldova evidence is added.
rows.gap: A defendable Moldova market file should include model-level GB/T-to-IEC mapping, connector and cable compatibility mapping for Type 2 / CCS2, interconnection and charging-service obligations, OCPP version and security profile, local language labels and manuals, operator and maintenance responsibilities, and an unresolved item list.

mandatory_status.target: Mixed: CE and electrical safety requirements are mandatory where in scope; ANRE interconnection and service obligations are mandatory for regulated charging operation; connector and backend requirements follow project, operator, or tender terms
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T baseline and domestic certification are preparatory references only, not direct Moldova market authorization

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build a Moldova-specific package after GB/T mapping rather than claiming full market readiness from China baseline documents alone.

rows.requirement: OCPP Backend Interoperability and EMI/EMC Interface
rows.target_requirement: Moldova charging projects may require OCPP compatibility, communication security profiles, and backend interoperability for operators and tariff settlement, together with electromagnetic compatibility practices for station electronics. Open Charge Alliance documentation and project terms often define the acceptable OCPP version and security class.
target_standards: Applicable electromagnetic compatibility expectations for station equipment
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese DC chargers often use GB/T 27930 for charger-to-vehicle communication, but this is not a substitute for backend interoperability, cybersecurity, and operator acceptance required for Moldova operations.
china_standards: Operator backend protocol and cybersecurity requirements
rows.gap: The gap is defining OCPP scope and safety-electromagnetic design for the Moldova lane, including endpoint URLs, certificate handling, meter data mapping, transaction model, remote update process, and site network architecture.

mandatory_status.target: Usually mandatory when operator, tender, roaming, payment, or safety operation conditions specify OCPP and EMC acceptance; not itself a whole-unit safety certificate
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — GB/T 27930 cannot satisfy backend interoperability requirements

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm exact OCPP version, security profile, and interoperability evidence with the Moldova station operator before shipment. GB/T 27930 alone is insufficient for backend acceptance.

rows.requirement: CE Marking and TS EN IEC 61851 Safety File
rows.target_requirement: For Moldova-facing EV charging products, the expected baseline is a CE-aligned conformity file with Declaration of Conformity, technical documentation, installation manual, and risk analysis where applicable. IEC 61851-1:2017 is the central safety standard often referenced for conductive EV supply equipment, and mandatory status depends on ANRE route and project or tender requirements.
target_standards: CE marking for applicable EU-aligned product legislation
TS EN IEC 61851 series and Moldova applicability via ANRE / standards references
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB/T 18487.1 for conductive charging system general requirements and GB/T 20234 for connection equipment. These help with technical mapping but do not replace Moldova-required CE-style or ANRE-facing packages.
rows.gap: A China-based package should be reorganized into a Moldova-ready technical file with explicit CE scope statement, harmonized/adopted standards list, test traceability, installation and safety manuals, declaration evidence, and label artwork aligned with local language requirements.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the equipment is in CE-oriented scope and ANRE or project requirements require it, with TSE-adjacent acceptance potentially added by route
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — GB/T 18487 and GB/T 20234 are baseline references unless Moldova project rules make specific clauses mandatory

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Use IEC / TS EN IEC 61851 evidence as part of a Moldova CE-style technical-file route. Confirm ANRE, operator, and project-specific requirements before claiming market readiness.
